title: Flower Drum Song and TV series work
summary: Carter recounts arranging and orchestrating for Flower Drum Song and episodes of Bold Ones, Ironside, Night Gallery; TV and film mechanics are the same.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Well, I want to ask you about "The Flower Drum Song".
Yes?
Do you remember what you did there?
I didn't do a great deal. I did some arranging, some orchestrating, and I played in the orchestra.
Okay. Now on TV, your first work
Yes.
But you also worked on "The Bold Ones"
I did a couple of segments. Yes.
By a 'segment' you mean you did a couple of episodes.
Episodes, yes, that's right.
"Ironside".
Yes, a number.
Now what did you do with "Night Gallery"?
I did a couple of segments of that.
Was that a serial, I mean, something that went on week after week?
Yeah, with Rod Serling staying, (unintelligible).
Then the "Pearl Bailey Show" -- that was the recent show that she was on? She had a regular series about 3 years ago, was it?
Oh, maybe a little longer -- about '71-, '72. I guess.
Uh huh. And you did, not the ...
I did the arrangements.
Just the arrangements of particular tunes that she sang when the band played.
Right, uh huh.
Was there something called a "Markam"? Did you do a "Markam"?
"Markam" was a TV show at Universal, I probably did a segment of that.
Right. Do you find any difference between TV and ... what would you call them, theatrical films, or something?
No drastic difference, no.
Essentially, the technique and the work is the same.
The mechanics are pretty much the same.
You have a little bit more time with a theatrical film, or, you know, because it's a big studio, bigger band, usually.
Usually, yes.
And a bigger budget.
Yes. Oh yes.
And a little bit more time to work on it, but otherwise, the mechanics are pretty much ...
Yes, the mechanics are pretty much the same.
